screens.prompt: In B7, find the position of the month in B6 within A2:A5, counting the first row as 1.

hints.syntax: =MATCH(B6,A2:A5,0): the month to find, the list to search, then the match type.
hints.func-match: MATCH hands back a count of cells, 3. The units in B4 are INDEX's job.
hints.match-exact: Leave the third argument out and MATCH treats the month list as sorted. Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr is calendar order, so the answer cannot be trusted.
hints.require-ref: Take the month from B6. Typing Mar into the formula means April needs an edit to the formula, not the sheet.
hints.value: Jan is 1, Feb is 2, Mar is 3. Counting starts at the top of A2:A5, not the top of the sheet.
hints.error: A month that is not in A2:A5 returns #N/A. With the third argument at 0, MATCH will not guess at a nearest row.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
without the third argument MATCH assumes an approximate search on a sorted list, which this column is not
a match type of 1 is approximate even though it happens to answer 3 today, and it would stop agreeing the moment a month was inserted
MATCH already counts the first row as 1, so adding one reports position four
the month typed into the formula, so the question can no longer be changed from the sheet
the searched range stops at Feb, so Mar is not in it and MATCH returns #N/A

docs.explain:
MATCH counts how far down a list a value sits. The months in A2:A5 run Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, and B6 holds Mar, so MATCH returns 3. That 3 is a position inside A2:A5, which is row 4 on the sheet.

The third argument decides how much tolerance MATCH allows. A zero asks for an exact match and is the safe choice here, because Jan to Apr is calendar order and approximate search assumes ascending sort. Set 1 and MATCH returns the last entry it judges to be at or below the value.

A month that is not in the list returns #N/A. There is no position for a value the list does not hold, so anything built on MATCH fails visibly. INDEX, in the next exercise, takes this 3 and reads the third cell of another column.

errors.text: No cell in A2:A5 holds the month, so MATCH has no position to return.
The searched range was a block rather than one row or column, or the match type was text.
The match type was left out or set to 1, so MATCH searched a calendar-order list as though it were ascending and picked a neighbouring month.

docs.atWork: Feeding a row number to INDEX without typing 3 into the formula by hand.
docs.outcome: Find where a value sits in a list, counting the first cell as 1.

seo.title: MATCH in Excel: find a value's position
seo.description: Mar is the third entry of Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, so MATCH answers 3. The third argument 0 demands an exact match, and 1 needs a list sorted ascending.
